title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Retention, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence & Exceptions
author: Asha Patel
summary: Consolidated security and compliance reference that defines RBAC and authentication standards, audit logging requirements and pipeline SLOs, data residency and retention policies, secure SDLC gates, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and the risk & exceptions process for Redwood Inference.
body:
Overview

This document consolidates the security and compliance controls that apply to Redwood Inference production and customer-facing systems. It is intended for engineering owners, platform and SRE teams, product, and security reviewers. The goal is to ensure consistent enforcement of least privilege, reliable audit trails, clear data residency and retention commitments, secure development practices, repeatable incident security operations, and a documented process for compliance evidence and risk exceptions.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood-owned services, managed private deployments, and any customer-specific infrastructure where Redwood provides control-plane functionality.
- Key topics: RBAC & auth, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response (security-focused), compliance evidence workflows, risk & exceptions.

Ownership and Contacts
- Document owner: Security team (security@redwood.internal).
- RBAC & Auth owner: Identity team (identity@redwood.internal).
- Audit logging & evidence pipelines: Observability team (observability@redwood.internal).
- Data residency & retention policy owner: Legal & Security (privacy@redwood.internal).
- Incident triage (security-focused): Incident Response team (ir@redwood.internal).
- Emergency on-call: see /confluence/eng-sre/dashboards-and-alerts for on-call roster.

Principles (high level)
- Least privilege: grant the minimal role required and review roles quarterly.
- Auditability: all privileged actions and data-access events must be logged and retained per the retention table below.
- Separation of duties: deploy and approve policies should not be held by same person where feasible.
- Region-aware controls: enforce data residency for customer-controlled data based on contracts and region tags.

1) RBAC and Authentication
Purpose: Ensure consistent, least-privilege access across control plane, internal services, and customer-managed private deployments.

Key services and systems
- Identity provider: identity.redwood.internal (OIDC + SCIM sync to cloud providers).
- Auth service: auth-service (internal microservice handling token issuance and policy evaluation).
- Cloud IAM: AWS Organizations and GCP IAM with provider mappings.

Standard roles (examples)
- role:platform-admin | scope:global | brief:Full control of deployment pipelines and infra | owner:eng-infra
- role:service-owner | scope:service-level | brief:Manage service config and rollouts | owner:service-team
- role:read-only | scope:org | brief:View-only access to dashboards and logs | owner:observability
- role:auditor | scope:logs | brief:Access to audit logs and evidence bundles | owner:security

Role lifecycle and review
1. Create role request via identity.redwood.internal/requests with justification.
2. Approval required from role owner and security reviewer.
3. Quarterly review: automated report from identity-service lists active members and last use.
4. Auto-expire temporary roles after 90 days unless renewed.

Service-to-service auth
- Use mTLS for internal service RPCs where practical.
- Short-lived signed JWTs for cross-region requests via auth-service.

Privilege escalation policy
- Privilege escalation must be requested through the escalations workflow. All escalations are logged to audit pipeline and require an approval record.

2) Audit Logging
Purpose: Provide tamper-evident, searchable trails for security, compliance audits, and incident forensics.

Required events (minimum)
- Authentication events: login success/failure, token issuance, revocation.
- Authorization checks: policy decisions for critical APIs (create/delete/modify).
- Administrative actions: role changes, access grants, configuration changes.
- Data-access events: reads/writes for customer data classified as sensitive.
- Deployment and config changes: CI/CD pipeline approvals, deployment rollbacks.

Pipeline and storage
- Primary collectors: audit-collector (service) forwards events to:
  - Splunk Enterprise (splunk-enterprise) for long-term indexed search for security team.
  - Cloud provider native logs: AWS CloudTrail (management events) and GCP Cloud Audit Logs for provider-level events.
- Delivery SLO: 99.9% of audit events available in Splunk within 2 minutes of generation.
- Integrity: daily retention integrity check job (audit-integrity-checker) verifies checksums and writes a signed manifest to S3 (s3://redwood-audit-manifests).

Retention and access
- Default retention (internal): 1 year in hot index, 3 years in cold index, 7 years archived (encrypted-at-rest).
- Customer contractual retention: obey data residency and retention commitments in customer contract (see Data Residency section).
- Access controls: only 'auditor' and authorized SOC roles can access raw audit indices. All access is logged.

Log format and required fields (JSON example)
- timestamp, event_id, principal_id, principal_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, request_id, trace_id, ip, user_agent, region, risk_score

3) Data Residency & Retention
Purpose: Ensure customer data is stored and retained according to contract and regulatory requirements.

Residency boundaries
- Region tags defined at resource creation time. Examples: eu-west-1 (for EEA), us-east-1 (NA), ap-southeast-1 (APAC).
- Control plane metadata (deployments, billing) may be global; sensitive customer payloads must be pinned to configured residency region.

Retention policy (summary table)
- Customer-managed: as specified in contract (common tiers: 90 days, 1 year, 7 years).
- Default platform: user-content (non-sensitive) = 90 days; logs/telemetry = 1 year hot / 3 years cold; audit logs = 7 years archived.

Retention schedule and deletion process
1. Owner configures retention via Console or API (route: /api/v1/retention).
2. Retention service validates policy and writes expiry metadata to retention-store (s3://redwood-retention-metadata).
3. Expiry job runs nightly and issues deletions under supervised transaction with kinesis-deletion-queue.
4. Deletion verification report generated monthly and sent to privacy@redwood.internal.

Edge cases
- Legal hold: Legal can request immediate suspension of deletions for a given tenant; requests are routed to privacy@redwood.internal and are logged to audit pipeline.
- Cross-region replication: disabled for data marked with "region-prohibition" tag.

4) Secure SDLC (development and deployment controls)
Purpose: Integrate security gates into the development lifecycle to reduce vulnerabilities in production.

Gates and tooling
- Code review: mandatory for all changes to services handling customer data.
- Static analysis: SAST runs in CI on merge requests (tool: secure-scan).
- Dependency scanning: weekly SCA scans with automatic PRs for high severity findings (tool: dep-watch).
- Secrets scanning: pre-commit and CI secrets scanner (tool: secret-guard).
- Dynamic testing: scheduled DAST on public endpoints (tool: dynamic-check).
- Infrastructure as code scanning: TFCheck in CI for terraform and k8s manifests.

Environments and access
- dev/staging/prod separation with network ACLs and RBAC.
- Service accounts used for deployments with least privilege; humans cannot use service account keys directly.

Release approvals
1. Automated test pass (unit/integration/security gates).
2. Canary rollout: 10% traffic for 2 hours with health checks.
3. Full rollout: progressive increase with automatic rollback on error budget breach (>1% error rate sustained >10m).
4. Post-deploy security scan: quick vulnerability sweep within 24 hours.

5) Incident Response \u2014 Security Procedures (IR-Sec)
Purpose: Provide playbooks for incidents that have a security impact (data exposure, authentication compromise, critical service breach).

Classification and severity
- Sev1 (Critical): confirmed data exfiltration of customer-sensitive data, production-wide authentication compromise, or full cluster compromise.
- Sev2 (High): targeted customer impact, leaked credentials with evidence of use, or lateral movement detected.
- Sev3 (Medium): isolated failure with minor security implications.

Initial containment steps (numbered procedure)
1. Detect & Triage: IR lead (ir@redwood.internal) to classify and notify SRE and CISO within 15 minutes of detection.
2. Preserve Evidence: snapshot relevant hosts/containers, preserve audit logs and network captures to evidence-bucket (s3://redwood-ir-evidence) and do not modify.
3. Contain: rotate affected credentials, revoke tokens issued by auth-service for compromised principals, isolate impacted services via network ACLs.
4. Communicate: notify internal stakeholders and legal; if customer data affected, notify customers per legal templates and SLA timelines.
5. Recover: follow tested runbooks for service restore; do not re-enable accounts until post-incident remediation complete and verified.

Forensics and post-incident
- Forensics owner: IR team. All analysis notes are added to incident timeline and retained in the incident tracker (internal ticket ID).
- Post-incident review: security and SRE co-author remediation plan and owner list, with completion targets (30/60/90 days).

Notification thresholds
- Any confirmed data exposure of PII triggers customer notification within 72 hours unless legal advises otherwise.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Purpose: Define how to collect, store, and present evidence for audits (SOC2, ISO, customer audits).

Evidence types and owners
- Access control evidence: role definitions, user lists, access reviews — owner: Identity team.
- Audit logs: indexed logs and integrity manifests — owner: Observability.
- SDLC evidence: CI/CD logs, SAST/DAST results — owner: Eng-Developer-Experience / Security.
- Incident evidence: incident timeline, postmortem, attestations — owner: Incident Response.

Evidence collection process (high level)
1. Evidence request received by compliance@redwood.internal.
2. Owning team pulls artifacts into evidence-bundle tool which captures checksums and timestamps.
3. Evidence bundle stored in secured evidence store (s3://redwood-evidence) with restricted access and tamper-evident manifests.
4. Reviewer signs evidence with platform key (kms-redwood) and updates audit-tracker.

Retention of evidence
- Evidence related to audits is retained per regulatory obligations; typical baseline is 7 years for audit artifacts.

7) Risk and Exceptions
Purpose: Define a formal risk-acceptance and exception process for controls that cannot be implemented immediately.

Exception request workflow (numbered)
1. Submit exception request via security-exceptions (confluence form link) with justification, compensating controls, and proposed duration (max 180 days).
2. Security triage: Security reviews category, impact, and recommends mitigations.
3. Approval board: CISO and service owner approve or deny; high-risk requests routed to legal for contract risk assessment.
4. If approved, owner must provide monitoring and compensating controls and schedule remediation milestones; request auto-expires and requires re-approval if not remediated.

Required fields for exception request
- Service name, control to be excepted, justification, compensating controls, proposed expiry date, test/monitoring plan, owner.

Auditability and reporting
- All exceptions are tracked in the exceptions registry and included in quarterly risk reports to executive leadership.

Appendix A \u2014 Example CLI and Queries
- Query last 24h failed logins (Splunk): index=audits action=auth_failure | stats count by principal_id, src_ip
- Revoke tokens for a principal (auth-service): curl -X POST https://identity.redwood.internal/api/v1/tokens/revoke -d '{"principal_id":"user-123"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>'
- Evidence bundle creation (example): evidence-tool create --service=auth-service --period=2028-06 --output=s3://redwood-evidence/auth-service-2028-06.bundle

Appendix B \u2014 SLA & SLO Highlights
- Audit delivery SLO: 99.9% within 2 minutes.
- Retention integrity check: daily, 100% of manifests verified; exceptions investigated within 24 hours.
- Incident notification: IR lead notified within 15 minutes of detection; customer notification for confirmed exposure within 72 hours.

Related pages and references
- Security control book: /confluence/security-and-compliance/security-and-compliance-controlbook-2027-10-01
- Incident response runbooks: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process
- Identity & access standards: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/infra-standards

Maintenance and review cadence
- This document reviewed quarterly or after any major program change.
- Owners must confirm their sections annually during the certification window.

Notes and exceptions
- Any deviation from the standards defined here must follow the Risk and Exceptions process and be recorded in the exceptions registry.
